LintSummary: [NOTE] {0} chars, {1} hit(s), {2} note(s), paragraph mode {3}. This command only reports locations; the actual rewriting is left to the judgment layer.
LintRule_ellipsis-style_Detail: Non-standard ellipsis: repeated Chinese full stops, or a single ellipsis character (the standard form is ……). Three or more ASCII dots are not reported, since code and old terminals use them everywhere
LintRule_mixed-punctuation-width_Detail: Half-width punctuation next to Chinese or full-width characters
LintRule_invisible-characters_Detail: Invisible characters (zero width / soft hyphen / no-break space)
LintRule_ai-frequent-words_Detail: High density of AI frequent words
LintRule_vague-attribution_Detail: Claim attributed to a vague source
LintRule_training-cutoff-disclaimer_Deta: The model cites its knowledge cutoff: that is about how far its own knowledge goes, not about when the facts were true; "data as of 2019" in a paper or a news report does not count
LintRule_sycophancy_Detail: Lifting the other person up before speaking: praising the question, praising their eye for detail, writing a reply as catching the person. The reader wants an answer, not to be caught. It keys on 好问题 with an exclamation mark right after it; 修好问题 hits the same way, since the words in front are not looked at, so read every hit once more
LintRule_elevated-ending_Detail: Paragraph raised to a lofty close
LintRule_copula-avoidance_Detail: Complex structure used instead of 是/有
LintRule_inline-title-list_Detail: List item with a bold title plus colon
LintRule_forced-reversal_Detail: Bare "反而": forced reversal without a concession; hits are candidates, read the context
LintRule_accounting-cliche_Detail: "Do the math" style cliche: data introduced by an invented action
LintRule_accounting-word-misuse_Detail: "记一笔" is bookkeeping wording: 笔 counts ledger entries, and you tally one only while keeping accounts. For an event write "值得一记", not "值得记一笔". Only the 值得…记一笔 shape is caught: balances, expenses and grudges are real bookkeeping and stay quiet. The shape shows up once in this workspace and it was written by a model; human-written text has none
LintRule_mixed-quote-style_Detail: Full-width and half-width quotes mixed (nesting one style inside another does not count)
LintNote_paragraph-length-uniform: Paragraph lengths are too uniform (coefficient of variation {0}, {1} paragraph(s)); human-written text usually varies more
LintRule_paragraph-length-uniform_Detail: Paragraph lengths are too uniform (coefficient of variation {0}, {1} paragraph(s)); human-written text usually varies more
LintNote_sentence-length-uniform: Sentence lengths are too even (coefficient of variation {0}, {1} sentence(s))
LintRule_sentence-length-uniform_Detail: Sentence lengths are too even (coefficient of variation {0}, {1} sentence(s))
LintNote_exclamation-density: High exclamation mark density: {0} mark(s) / {1} char(s)
LintRule_exclamation-density_Detail: High exclamation mark density: {0} mark(s) / {1} char(s)
LintNote_ordinal-skeleton: Ordinal skeleton "first/next/finally" appears {0} time(s), a typical trace of structured formatting
LintRule_ordinal-skeleton_Detail: Ordinal skeleton "first/next/finally" appears {0} time(s), a typical trace of structured formatting
LintNote_explicit-numbering: Explicit numbering markers: {0}, a typical trace of structured formatting
LintRule_explicit-numbering_Detail: Explicit numbering markers: {0}, a typical trace of structured formatting
LintNote_short-sentence-run: {0} sentences in a row within {1} characters: metronomic fragments, as if actions and feelings were filled in one by one
LintRule_short-sentence-run_Detail: {0} sentences in a row within {1} characters: metronomic fragments, as if actions and feelings were filled in one by one
HintLintRuleAlgorithmRule: Whether this rule fires is computed in code: there is no entry list to edit, and the match type and per-paragraph minimum are fixed there too. What you can change here: title, note, severity, text types, and whether it is off by default.
HintLintRuleEdit: Pick a rule on the left, edit it on the right. One entry per line; regex uses .NET syntax. Leave all three text types unchecked to apply the rule everywhere. Edited entries are written to lint_rules.json next to the program; restoring removes the entry from that file.
MsgLintRulePatternsEmpty: At least one entry is required.
MsgLintRuleMinCount: The per-paragraph minimum must be a positive integer.
LintRulePresetSummary: {0} checked, {1} apply to this genre, {2} rules in total
LintRuleDeleteConfirm: Delete rule "{0}"? Built-in rules can only be unchecked; custom rules are removed from the rule file.
LintRule_choppy-clauses_Detail: {0} clipped clauses averaging {1} characters, joined by semicolons and dashes: the subject and object are gone, so the reader has to fill them in
LintRule_repeated-verbatim_GroupDetail: {0} consecutive sentences from here match line {1}, column {2} onward word for word
LintRule_fiction-sensation-tics_Detail: Feelings written as ready-made noun phrases: falling into an ice cave, mind going blank, a puppet on strings. The reader gets a label, not anything concrete. Real writers also use these, so this rule only hints
LintRule_fiction-synonym-chain_Detail: Two near-synonymous clauses side by side in one paragraph: the reader gets the same thing twice. Needs two in a paragraph; a single one is ordinary writing
LintRule_fiction-proportion-eyes_Detail: Feelings sliced into fractions: one part disdain, two parts displeasure, three parts coldness. The reader gets a pie chart legend instead of a person. Needs two in a paragraph
LintGroupHeaderDense: [Hit] {0} ({1} hits, {2} per 1000 chars): one template repeating, samples only
LintRule_fiction-text-self-reference_Tit: Pointing back at its own lines
LintRule_fiction-text-self-reference_Det: The story turns around to point at the lines it just wrote. The reader is following a character, not proofreading your draft. Human novels: 0.01 per 1k characters; drafts like this: 8.8
LintRule_fiction-metaphor-lexicon_Detail: These vehicles have been used to death: the reader has seen them a thousand times and gets a template instead of a picture. Human novels peak at 0.32 per 1k characters; drafts like this: 18.7
LintRule_agent-one-char-commitment_Detai: 「我认」「我接」「我跟」「我记下了」used as a whole sentence turn commitment into a reflex and end the turn there. The reader needs to know which item is accepted, what is taken on, where the agent follows
LintRule_agent-receipt-commitment_Title: A receipt instead of a fix
LintRule_agent-receipt-commitment_Detail: 「我记下了」「记在账上」swap an admission for a receipt: nothing is admitted, the message is only logged, and the fix is deferred. Same family as 「我认」, one step later — the reader still gets an acknowledgement instead of the next move. Only the closing shape counts; 「我记一下电话」takes an object and stays a normal sentence
LintRule_agent-template-preamble_Detail: Praise the observation, then 「但需指出」, then first/second/in addition, then 「我可以承认…但不等于」: four floors of nothing, and the reader still cannot tell which sentence changes. Deleting the whole block usually loses no information
LintRule_agent-weight-comparison_Detail: Ordinary talk gets weighed: 「这句话比之前的都重」「比刚才稳」. Heavier, lighter, steadier describes the speaker's attitude, not the thing; the reader still cannot check a single fact
LintRule_agent-keepsake_Title: Keeping the sentence as a keepsake
LintRule_agent-keepsake_Detail: 「这话我收下了」「这句我留着」「收不回去」: the other person's words are filed as a keepsake. It sounds weightier than 「我记下了」 and still never says what changes next
LintRule_agent-measure-invite_Title: Telling the reader to weigh it
LintRule_agent-measure-invite_Detail: Instead of saying「你定」, the choice is handed back as 「你自己掂量」: a tone of authority laid over the same non-answer. The reader wants the options and what each costs; a decision goes through the questionnaire tool
LintRule_agent-caretaker-line_Detail: 「回去睡」「睡吧，我守着」「不催你」「你去，我跟」: a question about a failing function gets staged as a bedside scene. The reader wants the line to change, not goodnight
LintRule_agent-probe-question_Detail: The question is not answered, it is turned back inside the asker: 「问别人还是问自己」「是你自己想明白的」「什么心思都写着…」. The asker wanted a fact; the probe moves the topic off it
LintRule_agent-bare-verb-closer_Title: A transitive verb left at the end
LintRule_agent-bare-verb-closer_Detail: A transitive verb closes the clause with no object: caught what, steadied which step, knew which way back. The reader has to supply it, and when nothing fits, only a tone is left. Engineering compounds are excluded by the character in front: connected up, joined on, plugged in, and keeping an object around
LintRule_fiction-dialogue-reference_Titl: Dialogue keeps pointing at the last line
LintRule_fiction-dialogue-reference_Deta: The characters keep commenting on what the other just said instead of acting or answering, so the conversation turns into a review of the wording. Human novels peak at 0.44 per 1k characters; drafts like this run 8 to 20
LintRule_fiction-narrator-formula_Detail: The storyteller's opening and closing formulas are packed into one piece: every label of the old chapter-tale register pasted on at once. Real chapter tales spread them across the opening and close of each chapter: the whole of Water Margin runs 0.79 per 1k characters, its densest single chapter 1.86. Drafts like this run 7.9. Only markers at the start of a sentence or paragraph count, so 'he left the sentence half said' does not
LintNote_sentence-tempo: From line {0}: {1} sentences in this window, {2} characters on average, the longest {3}: nothing is ever said at length, the passage hammers along
LintRule_sentence-tempo_Detail: From line {0}: {1} sentences in this window, {2} characters on average, the longest {3}: nothing is ever said at length, the passage hammers along
LintRule_fiction-simile-pile_Detail: One sentence of {0} characters strings together {1} similes: the reader gets a row of vehicles instead of a picture. Human novels stay under 0.08 such sentences per 1k characters
LintRule_triadic-parallel_Detail: Three or more items in a row, each opening with the same character. The parallelism carries tone, not content: the reader remembers the rhythm and nothing else. Human novels stay under 0.10 per 1k characters; drafts like this run 8.5
LintRule_agent-agreement-opener_Detail: The reply starts a sentence by agreeing before saying anything of its own, so the agreement becomes an opening line. Only sentence-initial and paragraph-initial agreement counts; reported speech does not. Human novels stay under 0.002 such openers per 1k characters
LintRule_agent-deliberation-leak_Title: Thinking out loud in the reply
LintRule_agent-deliberation-leak_Detail: The reply narrates its own deliberation: what the user is asking, how long the answer should be, whether to think first. The reader wants the answer, not the walk there
LintRule_terminology-pile_Detail: {0} such terms per 1k characters outside quotation marks: the terms replace concrete observation, so the reader gets nouns instead of anything seen. Human novels stay under 0.05 per 1k characters
LintRule_agent-reassurance-pile_Detail: 'I've got you', 'you've hit the core of it', 'you'll see clearly now' one after another: the reader wants an answer, not to be soothed. Human novels of 47 million characters use these phrasings 8 times in total
LintRule_agent-self-intro_Detail: Opening by stating what it is and that it is being honest: the reader wants the answer. Human novels use the Chinese phrase for "as an assistant" twice, meaning a helper, not this self-description
LintRule_agent-error-paste_Detail: Verbatim API error text means the passage was assembled from chat-window output rather than written. None appears in 48.8 million characters of human novels
LintRule_agent-flattery_Detail: Opening with "you are sharp" praises the person, not the question, and the answer that follows is usually empty
LintRule_agent-conclusion-preamble_Detai: "In one sentence" and "let me tell you the conclusion" back to back: the announcement carries no information; write the sentence instead
LintRule_no-debt-declaration_Detail: Announcing "nothing pending", "all cleared", "none outstanding" inside the body leaves a plaque for something that is not there: the reader wants to know what is still pending, not to read a clearance certificate. If nothing is left, drop the line; an empty table is empty.
LintRule_completion-log_Detail: Recording "already changed", "fixed last round", "acceptance passed" in the body: the reader needs the rule as it stands now; how it got there belongs in the change log, and leaving it here guides later readers back to the old state after any compression or paraphrase.
LintRule_supersession_Detail: Setting "was A, now B" against each other in the body: the reader needs to know what it is now. Once the old value is written down it is easy to quote as current after compression or paraphrase, and whoever wrote it is long gone.
LintRule_tombstone-of-deletion_Detail: A tombstone for something deleted -- "original cleared", "no longer on disk", "not here". The reader gets an epitaph instead of the content; write what is missing as missing, and put the destination in the change log where it can be looked up.
LintRule_re-report-suppression_Detail: Declaring "not a defect", "stop counting this as debt", "agreed boundary" up front: the next reader gets a prohibition, not a criterion. State the boundary as a condition -- when it does not apply -- so they can judge for themselves without knowing what a previous reader reported.
LintBaselineHeader: {0} hits beyond the baseline, {1} in the baseline
LintRule_dash-run_Detail: Two or more dashes in one paragraph: interrupting yourself again and again is a performed pause, while a single aside is enough. Agent replies report one dash, which dash-pause-in-reply covers
LintRule_dash-pause-in-reply_Detail: A dash used to fake a pause in an agent reply is reported even once: that is tone written as content. Asides in narration do not count
LintRule_tilde-run_Detail: Using ~ as an ellipsis or a tone marker is common in web fiction and is plain layout noise in documents
LintRule_foreign-script-mix_Detail: Cyrillic, Greek, Hangul, accented Latin or kana inside Chinese text: usually a model writing an interjection in another language
LintRule_char-face_Detail: Characters outside the allowed set: only printable ASCII, Han characters and full-width Chinese punctuation pass. Arrows, box drawing, geometric shapes, circled numbers, the approximate sign, the multiplication sign and the yuan sign have no glyph or the wrong width in old console fonts, so whole lines shift. Emoji, invisible characters, foreign letters, curly quotes, dashes and ellipses have their own rules and are not counted here
LintRule_deck-speak_Detail: Words like cost cutting, efficiency gains, empowerment and leverage points: two in a paragraph are reported. That is how you talk to colleagues; the reader wants the concrete action and what it cost
LintRule_fiction-modifier-chain_Detail: Four layers of modifiers chained in one sentence, with enumeration commas in between: the noun is buried at the end, so the reader only learns who is meant at the last character. Two layers is ordinary writing; four is a pile
LintRule_adverb-overuse_Detail: The same adverb keeps coming back within one paragraph (two are needed to report it): once is ordinary, in a row it is straining
LintRule_violent-verbs_Detail: Writing code changes as cutting, slashing, nailing or biting: an aggressive tic replaces the concrete action, so the reader gets tough talk instead of a change. Only counted in programming docs and agent replies, where a blade or a bite in fiction is literal and would report every fight scene. Guarded against 一刀切, 咬定, 咬合 and 最阴凉
LintRule_hedging-ending_Detail: The ending never lands: sales-style closers and all-purpose good wishes leave the reader unsure what to do next
LintRule_disclaimer-stack_Detail: Three or more disclaimers in one paragraph affirm nothing and deny nothing, so the reader gets no conclusion. One is fair caution; a stack is evasion
LintRule_hedge-denial-pile_Detail: Three 不代表, 不意味着 or 不能证明 in a row in one paragraph: three negations hung on one sentence leave the reader without a conclusion. Real writers do it too, since each denial in a parallel argument carries its own subject, and this rule cannot tell that apart, so read every hit once more. One is caution; a run is usually dodging
LintRule_anthropomorphic-subject_Detail: Making inanimate things ask, say or hope: the subject should be a person, and the result reads as translationese
LintRule_doc-process-residue_Detail: Progress narration inside a current-state doc (what phase one added, what is left for later, was A now B): once the task doc is gone the information hangs in the air, and after any compression it leads a model back to the old state. Such sentences are fine inside a change log
LintRule_assistant-persona_Detail: Laying process, rules and self-reference out as content (opening up every step, three rules first, the comment section is my meeting room, deep in thought). It takes a phrasing, not a word: fish, whales or a master persona come and go with the character and do not make an AI voice
LintRule_meta-commentary-marker_Detail: Signposts instead of content: looked at another way, what this really reflects, the deeper question. Guarded against 我们换个人来
LintRule_fiction-body-tics_Detail: Fixed pairings of expression, gesture and tone: the cheapest set of words for writing emotion, and they fit any character at all
LintRule_fiction-physio-tics_Detail: Pupils contracting, breath catching, freezing on the spot, reason collapsing: emotion written as vital signs, so the reader gets a chart instead of a feeling
LintRule_fiction-permission-consoling_De: But that does not mean you have to stay there forever, or you can talk it over with them: the worries are held down for the reader and then a permit is handed over. The permit has to name a concrete place to go; a vague 你可以 does not count. Human corpus: 10 in 46.96 million characters, set from reader consensus rather than a human-versus-model diff
LintRule_fiction-choice-diagnosis_Detail: Either you no longer want to manage that much, or you finally see you never liked ordering people around: a motive the other person never stated is spelled out for them and wrapped as a choice. Human corpus: 50 of this shape, mostly reporting someone else's thoughts; set from reader consensus rather than a human-versus-model diff
LintRule_fiction-beat-action_Detail: He paused and spoke again, he blinked, his expression slowly eased: a small gesture standing in for punctuation. Human drafts do it too (69 in 46.96 million characters) and one is invisible, so this only hints; the signal is a micro-gesture opening every paragraph of one reply
LintRule_fiction-atmosphere-props_Detail: Stagnant air, haze, curling steam, beads of sweat: props standing in for atmosphere. Two in a paragraph count; one is plain description, several are a stage set
LintRule_fiction-dominant-register_Detai: Possessiveness, an unquestionable tone, staring someone down, a husky voice: the posture vocabulary of the dominant party. Only collocations count, since single words like presence or low would flood the report
LintRule_fiction-filler-modifiers_Detail: Three intensifiers in one paragraph: one is measure, several are padding
LintRule_fiction-dead-metaphor_Detail: A metaphor used so often that the reader knows what comes next, which is the same as not writing it
LintRule_fiction-emotion-telling_Detail: Saying outright what a character has understood, or previewing it for the reader, instead of showing it through action and scene
LintRule_fiction-vague-nominalization_De: There is a kind of something in it: it never says who fails to understand or what they fail to understand, and the vagueness comes from omission
LintRule_fiction-vague-simile_Detail: A simile that can be moved to any scene: it carries no narrative work and only supplies mood
LintRule_fiction-community-taste_Detail: Pebbles dropped in a lake, pursed lips, wrung hands, knuckles and nails going white: readers already flinch at these. The pebble family needs a simile marker or has to land in the heart-lake, the nail family has to land on a palm or the character's own skin, otherwise they cannot be told apart from plain realistic action. Real drafts use them too, so this rule rests on community consensus rather than a human-versus-model diff
LintRule_latin-word-in-cjk_Detail: An English adverb or adjective inside a Chinese sentence (he subtly stepped back half a step). Fan translations of names and brand names hit too, so this only reminds
LintRule_fiction-bold-template_Detail: Bold markers in fiction prose, however short: published text does not emphasise that way, system prompts and verdict templates do
LintRule_fiction-machine-numbers_Detail: Decimals, percentages, time codes, clause numbers: machines and official forms write numbers that way, while narration says seven or eight out of ten, or about two hundred. Chinese numerals are not counted
LintRule_synopsis-formula_Detail: The blurb skeleton (in a world full of X, an ordinary boy, discovers he has a mysterious power, begins his journey): swap the words and it fits any genre, so the reader finds nothing unique to this book
LintRule_trailer-ending_Detail: Pushing the outcome into the future at the end of a paragraph and leaving the answer for later (this is only the beginning, more unknowns await, the answer comes below): the reader gets a trailer, not a close. Human novels: 0.9 per million characters; these AI drafts: 28.5 per hundred thousand
LintRule_outline-residue_Detail: Numbered suspense and foreshadowing slots in the body (Suspense 1:, Foreshadowing:): fields of a planning prompt were output as prose. Human fiction never writes that way
LintRule_synopsis-register_Detail: Explore, conceal, journey, full of danger: summarising verbs replace concrete action and turn a scene into a blurb. The same sentence still works after swapping the genre, so the reader sees nothing unique to this book
LintRule_connective-scene-shift_Detail: An argumentative connective doing the work of a scene change (however, on one chance occasion ...), which flattens narration into staged explanation. Human novels: 0.48 per hundred thousand characters; these AI drafts: 36.6
LintRule_agent-commit-hash_Detail: Lowercase hex strings in the body (9f7761a, 2773ef7) that the reader cannot decode and simply skips. Agent replies: 86 per hundred thousand characters; human technical writing: 0. To point at a change, say what changed; a hash only helps when you really need that exact revision
LintRule_agent-code-list_Detail: Two or more short labels only insiders recognise in one paragraph (P1 P2 P6 / S1-S6 / C1-C6): the reader has no legend and gets a run of numbers. Agent replies: 113 per hundred thousand characters; human technical writing: 5. Describe what the item governs; put the label in parentheses or drop it
LintRule_agent-path-list_Detail: Two or more file paths or build artifact names in one paragraph (TextTool.Core/LintRule.cs, texttool.dll): the reader needs to know what happened in a file, not where it sits on this machine. Agent replies: 134 per hundred thousand characters; human technical writing: 23
LintRule_agent-cli-option_Detail: Options like --json or --genre scattered through the body are only useful at the prompt. Agent replies: 29 per hundred thousand characters; human technical writing: 0. Put a command in its own block and say in the sentence what it does
LintRule_agent-smoke-jargon_Detail: Smoke, smoke test: in-team test jargon that an outsider cannot read as run the main flow and see if it breaks. Agent replies: 20 per hundred thousand characters; human technical writing: 0. Say what was actually checked this time, who ran it and what counted as passing; the slang variant 一支烟 counts too
LintRule_agent-test-jargon_Detail: Two or more of case, assertion, unit test and regression in one paragraph: precise inside testing, pure decoding cost inside a reply. Agent replies: 41 per hundred thousand characters; human technical writing: 0. Saying which behaviour was checked and how it turned out saves the reader more than a word list; fixture counts only in a testing context, in the agent genre
LintRule_agent-process-jargon_Detail: Words coined inside this circle (closing out, landing on disk, caliber, tier, health check) that a first-time reader has to translate first. Agent replies: 91 per hundred thousand characters; human technical writing: 2. Gloss one in plain words on first use, or replace it
LintRule_agent-inline-code_Detail: Five or more backticked spans in one paragraph, all file names, commands and identifiers: the prose turns into alternating Chinese and machine words and the reader keeps switching gears. Agent replies: 397 per hundred thousand characters; human technical writing: 25. Keep only what the reader truly has to type; name the rest
LintRule_agent-truncated-path_Detail: A path with its middle replaced by an ellipsis (…/rule-map.md): the reader cannot find it and cannot paste it back into a terminal. Agent replies: 33 per hundred thousand characters; human technical writing: 0. Give the full path, or just the file name
LintRule_numbered-reference_Detail: Numbers used as signposts: the reader has only this passage and would need a table from somewhere else to decode them. Write the item itself, or just the conclusion
LintRule_agent-conclusion-first_Detail: The summary is pressed onto the opening, so the reader is handed a conclusion before the story. Tell it in order and the conclusion lands harder at the end
LintRule_agent-permission-ask_Detail: Decisions that belong to a person go through the questionnaire tool: a question in the prose has no options, leaves no record and costs a turn, so any hit sends it back. Only the shape of asking for a decision counts, not polite pleasantries
